newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares rose after two-straight losses and analysts saw another gain on Wednesday with the market cheered by Monday's sharp Dow rebound.
Analysts said any sharp short-term moves by the Dow could rub off on Poland but that the market's upside would be limited in the run-up to the September 21 parliamentary elections.
"It seems last week's sharp growth had a speculative character and profit-taking should bring the market to equilibrium," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Bank Pekao house.
The main market, currently at 16,564.7 points, had risen 14.5 percent in a six-session period.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 16,564.7 points and turnover fell 11.8 percent to 140.6 million zlotys ($40.3 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 59 to 43 with 12 stocks flat.
Some analysts said Polish shares were relatively cheap compared to neighbouring bourses such as Hungary's which rallied in recent months.
Others said significant gains were unlikely as large-cap banks which led the recent surge had largely worn out their growth potential.
Banks which bucked the recent trend and recorded strong July earnings on Monday were among Tuesday's top gainers.
Bank Gdanski rose 10 percent on Monday's news July net profit had risen to 9.8 million zlotys ($2.8 million) from 7.3 million ($2.1 million) a year ago, analysts said.
Automotive group Sobieslaw Zasada, up 9.4 percent, also benefited from good results while bank WBK, which rose nine percent, was also reacting to recent falls, they said.
